To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the implementation of the orbital advection algorithm removes the time step constraint imposed by the orbital velocity, and that this algorithm makes the truncation errors more uniform across a shearing box.

the shearing box algorithm conserves energy, momentum, and magnetic flux to better than 1% over hundreds of orbital periods, and is stable and accurate for the study of MHD turbulence over hundreds of scale heights.

the implementation of a second-order Crank-Nicolson scheme for the Coriolic and tidal gravity source term in the momentum equation and the orbital advection algorithm in the energy and magnetic induction equations, together with appropriate boundary conditions, are sufficient to ensure conservation of mass, momentum, energy, magnetic flux, and magnetic energy in the shearing box simulations to better than 1% for hundreds of orbits.

the implementation of the Shearing-Box approximation in a MHD code, with the goal of being able to perform long-term, high-resolution simulations of accretion flows.
the development and implementation of numerical techniques that enable the study of the nonlinear dynamics of accretions disks using the shearing box approach.
the development of a numerical method for the study of MHD flows in shearing boxes.
